detail.text: Inspect every handling unit for damage before moving it into the warehouse.
If the product itself is visibly damaged, post the affected quantity to blocked stock, label the handling unit, and do not mix damaged and undamaged units on one pallet.
If the outer packaging shows visible damage, refuse the delivery and note the reason on the delivery note before the driver leaves.

If the outer packaging is damaged but the product inside is intact, take photos of the damaged packaging, post the goods receipt to blocked stock, notify the QA inspector, and note the damage on the delivery note.
Photos must show the handling unit label and the damage, and be attached to the goods receipt in the WMS.

The situation does not say whether the product itself is damaged or whether only the outer packaging is damaged, nor whether the product inside is intact. This matters because the passages give different handling instructions; if the outer packaging is visibly damaged and the product is intact, one passage says to refuse the delivery while another says to accept it.
Notify the QA inspector if the product itself is visibly damaged or if the outer packaging is damaged while the product inside is intact.
